claim: Plage de la Grande Mer is the main town-center beach near the port, fine sand with gentle-slope clear-water entry, with showers, paid toilets, wheelchair access and a summer lifeguard, and it is the most popular and crowded beach.
quote: Grande-Mer Beach - Surface: Fine sand - Location: Town center, near port and restaurants - Facilities: Showers, toilets (fee), wheelchair access, lifeguard in summer - Crowding: Popular, especially in peak season

claim: Plage du Bestouan is a 150m golden-pebble beach a 5-minute walk west of the center, supervised in summer but with no showers or toilets, and offers a panorama of Cap Canaille.
quote: Bestouan Beach - Surface: Golden pebbles (150m long) - Location: 5-minute walk from center - Facilities: Supervised in summer; no showers/toilets ... Offers exceptional panorama of Cap Canaille

claim: Anse du Corton is a quiet sand-and-pebble cove about 15 minutes east of the port with only a summer snack stand and a rocky entry where water shoes are advised.
quote: Corton Beach (Anse du Corton) - Surface: Fine sand and pebbles (less comfortable) - Location: 15 minutes east of port - Facilities: Snack stand in summer; no showers/toilets - Water: Gentle slope but rocky; wear water shoes - Crowding: Relatively quiet

claim: Plage de l'Arène is a rocky, sand-free, unsupervised beach about 20 minutes east of the port that is rarely visited, allows dogs year-round, and requires water shoes.
quote: Arena Beach (Plage de l'Arène) - Surface: Rocks (no sand) - Location: 20 minutes east of port - Facilities: None; no showers/toilets - Water: Requires water shoes ... Crowding: Rarely visited; unspoilt oasis - Note: Dogs allowed year-round

claim: Calanque de Port-Pin has a fine-sand-and-small-pebble beach with transparent water reachable by a ~45-minute walk, has no facilities, and suffers from severe overcrowding in high season.
quote: Calanque de Port-Pin - Surface: Fine sand and small pebbles - Location: 45 minutes walk ... Facilities: None; bring picnic - Water: Transparent ... Crowding: Very busy in summer despite beauty - Note: suffers from overcrowding in high season

claim: Calanque d'En-Vau lies beyond Port-Pin (about a 40-minute further hike), is accessible only on foot or by kayak, and sees fewer visitors thanks to its difficult access; sea temperatures in the area range from 13°C in winter to 26°C in summer with swimming recommended June–October.
quote: Calanque d'En-Vau - Location: Beyond Port-Pin (40 minutes hike) ... Accessible only by foot or kayak ... Water temperature ranges from 13°C in winter to 26°C in summer. Swimming recommended June-October.

claim: The Cassis tourism office notes the bay is sheltered by Cap Canaille giving calm seas and crystal-clear, Blue Flag-certified water, with beach restaurants such as Same Same Beach and Comptoir de la Plage.
quote: The page emphasizes water quality through Blue Flag certification and describes the bay as being protected by Cap Canaille, offering calm seas, crystal-clear waters.

claim: Plage de la Grande Mer is a mix of sand and pebbles offering the most amenities including summer-supervised swimming, nearby restaurants and kayak/paddleboard rentals, and gets extremely busy in summer so early morning or late afternoon arrival is best.
quote: Plage de la Grand Mer does get extremely busy in the summer and you are best to either arrive early in the morning or later on in the afternoon ... It's a mix of sand and pebbles and offers the most amenities, including supervised swimming in summer, nearby restaurants, and water sports rentals like kayaks and paddleboards.

claim: TripAdvisor reviewers (4.1/5) describe Plage du Bestouan as a soft pebble beach with lovely clear water and excellent snorkeling (fish, octopus sightings) but say it gets packed in summer heatwaves like a sardine tin, and water can feel freezing in early June.
quote: Lovely clear water, great snorkelling ... so many fish ... packed on a Friday afternoon in a massive heat wave ... sardine bush, high season ... early June brought freezing water

claim: Cassis sea temperature averages about 20.8°C in June and peaks around 22.3°C in August, with the swimming season running June to October and water staying above 20°C through that period.
quote: June: average water temperature 20.8°C ... August has the highest average sea temperature at 22.3°C ... swimming season in Cassis lasts from June to October ... does not drop below 20°C
